problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U={2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is composite

- $Q(x):$ $10$ is divisible by $x$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/10d3d9a3b026fc1511d9e7a57c1f3276606c9397f0045fdb7748e3038a42fb21.png)

The shaded regions above represent the truth sets of predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ defined over the universal set ${R}^{2}.$ Which of the following is the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we have that 

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

 

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

First, we sketch the set ${T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/5dfcb1cff13cc5f5b6dcfa42a7e1d08184e54a7edd91717b795692068db37121.png)

Then, we sketch the set ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}$ and ${\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/3c4b6cd6b5649a18bd768b3086ccef5a995f9745a9ce90160507c9d92f46f8dc.png)

As a result, ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}$ is the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/62373d6926552c34849e91115163dba42483c6259482bc4893704af570749c89.png)

Finally, to get the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x),$ we take all the points that belong to ${T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q}$ or ${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099768/assets/252c206ca03b339c4bb186c95d21cd26110fc902f0ab9bca6df2d8d594aacba5.png)
